readerTitle: The bag you can't just buy: how Hermès guards its moat by saying no
caseNote: 실제 기업 (Hermès, LVMH 지분 사건, 2024년 미국 소송) + 가상 적용 (회사 안의 분석팀)
insight: 브랜드 해자는 더 많이 파는 데서가 아니라, 해자를 만든 원천(장인의 손)보다 빨리 자라지 않겠다는 절제에서 지켜진다.
misconception: 수요가 넘치면 생산을 늘리는 게 당연하다. 팔 수 있는 걸 안 파는 건 돈을 버리는 일이다.

sources.text: Hermès International, Universal Registration Documents (annual reports): craftsmanship model, leather workshops in France, artisan training
Hermès, brand history: the Birkin's origin with Jane Birkin and Jean-Louis Dumas (1984)
Reuters and Financial Times coverage of LVMH's stake in Hermès (2010) and the 2014 settlement
Reuters coverage of the 2024 California class-action lawsuit over Birkin sales practices

factChecks.note: Birkin 탄생(1984년, Jane Birkin과 Jean-Louis Dumas의 비행기 대화)은 Hermès 공식 자료와 다수 언론에 나오는 이야기이나 세부는 일화적 성격이 있어 카드에 'as the story goes'로 표시했습니다.
'가방 하나를 장인 한 명이 처음부터 끝까지 만든다'는 Hermès가 반복해서 밝힌 내용입니다. 제작 시간(보도마다 약 15~20시간)은 확실하지 않아 카드에서 '하루 이상의 작업'처럼 구체 수치 없이 썼습니다. 게시 전 확인하세요.
Hermès는 공식 대기자 명단이 없다고 밝혀 왔습니다. 카드에는 '공식 명단은 없다'와 '보도된 관행'으로 구분해 적었습니다.
LVMH의 지분 공개(2010년 10월)와 가문 지주회사(H51) 결성, 2014년 합의 후 LVMH의 지분 정리는 Reuters/FT 보도로 확인하세요. 지분율 수치는 카드에 넣지 않았습니다.
2024년 3월 캘리포니아 집단소송(버킨 구매를 위해 다른 제품 구매를 요구했다는 주장)은 소송 제기 사실만 적었고 결과는 쓰지 않았습니다. 게시 직전 진행 상황을 확인하세요.
재판매 가격이 매장가보다 높게 형성된다는 점은 널리 보도되었으나 배수는 시기·모델마다 달라 수치를 쓰지 않았습니다.

cards.title: The store that won't sell you the bag
body: Walk into a Hermès store and ask for a Birkin. You will usually leave without one.
Hermès says there is no official waiting list. Yet second-hand Birkins often sell for more than the store price. The company could make far more of them. For decades, it has chosen not to.

image.label: An empty, softly lit display shelf in a luxury store
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 고급 매장의 빈 진열대 하나에 조명만 비추고, 그 앞에 손님 실루엣 여러 명이 서 있음. 실제 Hermès 로고, 주황색 상자 디자인, 가방 형태의 상표 요소는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Demand is far bigger than supply.
body: You run a luxury leather house. Each of your top bags is made by one trained artisan, start to finish. Training takes years. Buyers line up, and resale prices beat yours.
Your board asks how to grow. What do you do?

options.text: Open new factories and use faster methods to meet demand
options.feedback: You capture years of sales quickly. But the bag stops being rare and hand-made, which is the reason people wanted it.

options.text: Keep supply where it is and raise the price until the line disappears
options.feedback: You take more money per bag and protect rarity. But a bag for anyone with enough cash loses some of its story, and big jumps can feel greedy.

options.text: Grow only as fast as you can train new artisans, and accept the unmet demand
options.feedback: You give up sales today. In return, the thing that makes the bag special stays intact, and the waiting keeps desire high.

cards.title: Growth at the speed of hands
body: The Birkin was born in 1984. As the story goes, actress Jane Birkin told Hermès chief Jean-Louis Dumas on a flight that she couldn't find a good weekend bag.

Hermès kept its top bags hand-made by single artisans, mostly in workshops in France. It adds capacity by opening new workshops and training craftspeople in its own schools, a slow process it describes in its annual reports.
Sales have grown for years. But **supply grows only as fast as skill does**.

cards.title: Guard the source of the moat
body: A moat protects profits from rivals. Every moat has a **source**: the thing that actually creates the advantage. For Hermès, the source is real craft and real rarity.
Growing past your source drains the moat. Each extra factory-made bag would add sales and subtract meaning.
So Hermès treats unmet demand not as lost money, but as **the moat's water level**.

image.label: A castle moat fed by a single spring labeled craft
image.brief: 인포그래픽. 성("Brand") 둘레의 해자에 물을 대는 샘 하나에 "Craft + rarity" 라벨. 옆에 "Grow faster than the spring" 화살표가 해자 물을 빼내는 파이프로 이어짐. 실제 로고 없음.

cards.title: The hard part is saying no
body: Other luxury makers can buy leather and hire artisans. What they find hard is refusing sales that investors expect.
A company that answers every surge in demand trains customers to expect the bag will always be there. Hermès trains them to expect the opposite.
The waiting itself becomes part of the product. Buying one says something that money alone can't.
cards.softwareNote: Software can copy itself for free, so the scarce source is usually something else: a curated community, hand-picked supply, or expert support. Invite-only launches work only while the scarcity is real. Opening the gates to chase growth can drain the very thing users joined for.

cards.title: The day a rival bought in
body: In 2010, luxury group LVMH revealed it had quietly built a large stake in Hermès. The founding family responded by pooling their shares into a holding company to keep control.
After a long dispute, LVMH agreed in 2014 to give up most of its stake.
The lesson: restraint is a strategy that needs owners willing to wait. A buyer chasing faster growth could have opened the factories.

cards.title: Scarcity can turn into resentment.
body: Unmet demand only helps when the product deserves it. Make something rare that nobody truly wants, and you just sell less.
Rationing also creates rules people may see as unfair. In 2024, a lawsuit in California challenged reported practices of steering Birkin buyers to spend on other products first.
Scarcity protects a moat while customers read it as craft. If they start reading it as a game, the brand can erode instead.

cards.title: Now it's a team inside a big company.
body: You lead a five-person analytics team. Leaders trust your reports because a senior analyst checks every number personally. Now requests have tripled.
How do you grow?

options.text: Take every request and skip the senior check on smaller ones
options.feedback: You serve more people this quarter. But one wrong number in a board deck can undo the trust that made everyone ask for you.

options.text: Accept fewer requests, and add capacity only as you train new reviewers to the same standard
options.feedback: Some teams will wait and grumble. You keep the review that is the source of your reputation, and grow it on purpose.

options.text: Hire contractors to handle the overflow under your team's name
options.feedback: It eases the queue fast. It works only if their work meets your check; otherwise your name carries their errors.

cards.title: Never grow faster than the thing that makes you special.
body: Find the source of your moat, then let it set the pace of growth. Some unmet demand is the price of keeping it.
**Try it today:** name the one thing customers can't get elsewhere from you. Write down what would happen to it if demand doubled tomorrow.
